plain: To bring a person into court to hear the charges and answer them

webster.text: To call or set a prisoner at the bar of a court, to answer to the matter charged against him in an indictment or information.

more.text: To accuse; to charge with faults.

example.quote: When he is arraigned for treason, he has the command of the army and navy, and may surround the Senate with thirty thousand troops.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 18, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
